title: Over 700 arrested in islandwide ‘Ratama Ekata’ operation - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - A total of 706 individuals were arrested yesterday (July 17) during the islandwide “Ratama Ekata” national operation.

According to Police, the arrests were made during 708 raids conducted across the country.

Among those arrested, an investigation into suspected illegally acquired assets has been launched against one suspect, while 11 others are being detained under detention orders for further investigations.

Police also said that steps have been taken to refer four suspects for rehabilitation.

title: House of Fashions owner remanded after Customs arrest - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - House of Fashions owner and Managing Director Preethi Jayawardena has been arrested over an alleged Customs violation and remanded while receiving treatment at the National Hospital in Colombo after developing a heart-related medical condition.

Sri Lanka Customs officers arrested Jayawardena at his residence during a special investigation into a customs valuation issue.

Customs senior official told the Daily Mirror Jayawardena developed a heart-related medical condition while in the custody of Customs officers and was subsequently admitted to the National Hospital in Colombo.

The Colombo Chief Magistrate later visited the hospital, observed the suspect, and ordered that he be remanded.

title: Kuwait International Airport suspends operations temporarily - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
(MediaSelangor) - Takeoff and landing operations have been temporarily suspended at Kuwait International Airport, Kuwait's national carrier announced on Saturday, adding that it rescheduled most of its flights due to the measure, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.

According to Bernama, Kuwait Airways in a statement said most flights have been rescheduled due to the temporary suspension of takeoffs and landings at Kuwait International Airport as a result of the Iranian aggression.

"Passengers are advised to stay updated on their flight status,” the carrier said.

The development came amid heightened tensions in the Middle East, where the United States launched strikes on Iran, and Tehran retaliates with strikes on regional countries, including Kuwait, which hosts US assets.

The exchange of fire between Washington and Tehran comes despite a Pakistan-brokered memorandum of understanding signed in June to end the war and reach a lasting peace agreement.

title: Roshan Mahanama clarifies Dambulla Sixers role amid conflict of interest concerns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - Former Sri Lanka cricketer Roshan Mahanama has clarified concerns raised over a possible conflict of interest regarding his role as team mentor of the Dambulla Sixers in the 2026 Lanka Premier League (LPL) and his position as a member of the Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) Transformation Committee.

Speaking at a media briefing, Mahanama said he was not involved with the Dambulla Sixers franchise in his capacity as a member of the Cricket Transformation Committee.

“There are concerns as to whether I can hold this role while being a member of the Cricket Transformation Committee.

Firstly, my appointment to the committee is on a temporary basis. I was not appointed through a vote or an official appointment by a federation,” he said.

Mahanama further explained that his involvement with the Dambulla Sixers and his responsibilities on the Transformation Committee were separate, while rejecting any suggestion of a conflict of interest.

title: Over 4,600 cases filed over mosquito breeding sites so far in 2026 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - Police have filed 4,672 court cases against individuals for maintaining premises conducive to mosquito breeding during the period from January to June 2026, the Police said.

In a statement, police said the legal action forms part of a nationwide special dengue control programme jointly conducted by the Ministry of Health, Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) and the Sri Lanka Police to curb the rapid spread of dengue.

Police noted that legal action can be instituted under Section 262 of the Penal Code against individuals who maintain mosquito breeding sites or keep their premises in an unhygienic condition that facilitates mosquito breeding.

The statement further said that under the Prevention of Mosquito Breeding Act, No. 11 of 2007, health authorities are legally empowered to issue Red Notices to owners or occupants of premises where mosquito breeding sites exist or where conditions are likely to encourage mosquito breeding due to poor sanitation.

title: Angolan woman nabbed at BIA with Rs. 10m cocaine concealed inside body - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - A 54-year-old Angolan woman has been arrested by the Sri Lanka Customs Narcotics Control Unit for allegedly attempting to smuggle cocaine worth more than Rs. 10 million into the country by concealing the drug inside her body.

The suspect arrived at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) on July 17 aboard Qatar Airways flight QR654 after travelling from Angola via Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and Doha, Qatar.

She was reportedly using a wheelchair upon arrival, which drew the attention of Customs officers.

During questioning, the woman voluntarily surrendered 14 capsules containing cocaine that had been concealed inside her body.

She also admitted to Customs investigators that she had swallowed several additional capsules containing the narcotic.

Customs said the recovered capsules contained a total of 237 grams of cocaine, with an estimated street value of more than Rs. 10 million.

Investigations are continuing.

title: Supermarket fined Rs. 1Mn for selling Keeri Samba above MRP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - A supermarket in Beruwala has been fined Rs. 1 million for selling locally produced Keeri Samba rice above the government-mandated Maximum Retail Price (MRP).

According to the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA), the supermarket had been selling Keeri Samba rice at Rs. 355 per kilogram, significantly higher than the gazetted MRP of Rs. 260 per kilogram.

During a raid, CAA officers found 5kg packs of the rice being sold for Rs. 1,775, exceeding the legally permitted price.

The CAA’s Kalutara District Investigative Officers filed legal action against the supermarket under the Consumer Affairs Authority Act.

When the case was taken up before by the Kalutara Magistrate’s Court on July 17, the defendants pleaded guilty, following which the Magistrate imposed a fine of Rs. 1 million.

title: Heat Index expected to reach caution level in several areas - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - The Department of Meteorology has issued a warm weather advisory for the Eastern Province and the districts of Jaffna, Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu, Vavuniya and Monaragala for today (18).

According to the advisory, the heat index — the temperature felt by the human body — is expected to rise to the ‘Caution’ level in some areas during the daytime.

The department advised the public to remain well-hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight where possible, and limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours of the day.

Authorities also urged residents to take necessary precautions to minimise heat-related health risks, particularly among children, the elderly and those engaged in outdoor work.

title: British mother accused of abducting sons from American father in cross-border custody dispute - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July 18 (Daily Mirror) - A British mother has been accused of abducting her two young sons from the United States after allegedly failing to return them to their American father following a court-approved visit to the United Kingdom, according to a report published by The Telegraph.

The woman, Nishika Samaratunga, 34, is at the centre of an international child custody dispute after allegedly keeping her two sons Blaine Baier, 5, and Nathaniel “Nate” Baier, 3 in Britain despite a court order requiring their return to the US.

According to The Telegraph, the children, who were born in the United States and lived with their father near Denver, Colorado, travelled to Britain in March to spend time with their mother following their parents’ separation.

They were scheduled to return to the US on March 29, but Samaratunga allegedly failed to take them to the airport as required. The children have not been located since, the report said.

The children’s father, Ben Baier, has initiated legal proceedings in the UK High Court seeking their return.

The dispute follows a custody battle in a Colorado court, where Samaratunga had reportedly sought permission to permanently relocate the children to London. The request was rejected, and the court later ruled that the father should become the primary custodial parent while allowing the mother contact with the children.

The father has raised concerns over the children’s welfare, particularly because both boys have autism and require stability in their education, healthcare, and daily routines.

The case highlights the growing complexity of international parental child abduction cases, where family disputes cross national borders and require cooperation between different legal systems.

Such cases are generally addressed through international mechanisms, including the 1980 Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, which seeks the prompt return of children wrongfully removed or retained across borders.

The convention aims to ensure that custody disputes are decided by courts in the child’s country of habitual residence rather than through unilateral decisions by either parent.

The case also reflects how private family disputes can become international legal matters involving child welfare, parental rights, and judicial cooperation between countries.

title: Dengue deaths in 2026 top 50, surpassing 2025’s total of 29 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has recorded 53 dengue-related deaths in the first seven months of 2026, already exceeding the 29 deaths reported during the whole of 2025, as the country's dengue outbreak continues to worsen with infections climbing to 73,455.

According to the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU), 50 dengue-related deaths have been reported as of July 16 this year, compared to 29 deaths recorded during the entirety of 2025.

The country has also recorded 73,455 dengue infections so far this year, with the official case fatality rate standing at 0.07%, reflecting the scale of the outbreak.

The Western Province continues to be the worst-affected region, accounting for more than half of all reported cases with 38,700 infections. Gampaha District has recorded the highest number of cases at 15,341, followed by Colombo with 14,625.

Furthermore, the Southern Province has reported 11,382 cases, while both the Sabaragamuwa and Central provinces have each exceeded 6,000 infections.

Health authorities said the outbreak has escalated rapidly over the past two months. June alone recorded 21,538 cases, while July has already added 18,076 cases by mid-month. In comparison, 8,590 cases were reported in May and 5,651 in April.

Moreover, the NDCU has identified 175 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas as high-risk during Epidemiological Week 27, with an average of 2,677 new cases being reported daily.

Health officials continue to urge the public to eliminate mosquito breeding sites, seek early medical attention for persistent fever and cooperate with vector control programmes.

title: PTA accused granted bail after 15 years - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - The Court of Appeal has granted bail to a man who had remained in remand custody for nearly 15 years under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), ruling that such prolonged pre-trial detention amounted to an exceptional circumstance warranting his release.

The Court held that the accused had spent approximately 15 years in detention before his bail application, adding that he was only 26 years old when he was arrested and had spent the prime years of his youth behind bars while awaiting trial.

The judgement, delivered by Justice Pradeep Hettiarachchi with Justice P. Kumararatnam concurring, set aside an order of the Colombo High Court which had refused bail to the third accused, Thambiah Prakash alias Dhanush, in a long-pending terrorism case.

The accused was arrested in August 2009 and indicted in September 2012 under the PTA and Emergency Regulations. The indictment contains 230 charges, 115 under the PTA and a further 115 under the Emergency Regulations and lists 106 prosecution witnesses.

Accordingly, the Court granted bail subject to stringent conditions, including a cash bail of Rs. 200,000, four sureties each signing a bond of Rs. 5 million, fortnightly reporting to the Counter Terrorism and Investigation Division at Police Headquarters, and the surrender of the accused's passport. The Court warned that any breach of the bail conditions would result in the cancellation of bail.

The Court observed that although Parliament introduced Section 15B to the PTA through the 2022 amendments, empowering courts to grant bail in exceptional circumstances, the High Court had failed to properly consider the legislative purpose behind the amendment when refusing bail.

The judgement further observed that the accused's daughter was only one year old at the time of his arrest and that his prolonged detention had deprived his family of his care and protection throughout that period.

Counsel Asthika Devendra with Aruna Madhusanka appeared for the accused. Deputy Solicitor General Anoopa De Silva appeared for the Attorney General.

title: Constable interdicted for allegedly sitting on WPC’s lap - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 18 (Daily Mirror) - A constable attached to the Makulugaswewa Police Station has been interdicted following allegations of misconduct involving a Woman Police Constable (WPC) while on duty.

According to the police, the incident occurred after the constable returned to the station from security duty at a musical concert held at the Dambulla Gamudawa Stadium on July 15. It is alleged that, upon returning to the station, the constable approached a female police constable who was seated and attempted to sit on her lap.

The WPC immediately reported the incident to the Officer-in-Charge (OIC), who informed the Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) in charge of the division. A preliminary inquiry was subsequently launched.

Investigations reportedly revealed that the constable was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident.

Following the inquiry, the ASP ordered the immediate interdiction of the constable pending further disciplinary action.
